correctness.rationale: For n>=8, exactly floor(log_2(n-2)) genuine chords (n,2^j) are added. With S_t=sum_{i=t}^n i, each target k in [n,T_n) lies uniquely in [S_t,S_{t-1}), so 0<=r=k-S_t<=t-2. Binary digits 2^j in r are distinct vertex labels below t, joined to suffix endpoint n by an existing cycle edge (j=0) or an added chord (j>=1). The chosen connected vertex set sums to k. Targets below n and T_n are immediate. The verifier independently checks all 88556 targets for n=3..80 and 956 larger samples. Boundaries n=8, t=2, t=n, r=0, k=T_n all follow. The finite tests do not replace the infinite proof.

value.rationale: A recently defined natural extremal invariant carried an explicit open question whether its n/2-size edge completion could be sublinear. A uniform O(log n) construction for every n>=8 resolves that question and gives an efficient canonical witness for every target sum. The result is an infinite structural improvement, not an arbitrary finite cutoff or a restatement of a textbook subset-sum lemma.
